title: Insurance-backed credits and contract template automation for high-risk enterprise onboarding
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: Large enterprise customers repeatedly request bespoke contract clauses and insurance indemnities. Negotiation time and legal review are a primary blocker to closing Dedicated/Private deals. Current onboarding is manual: account execs gather security questionnaires, engineering creates ad-hoc contract redlines, and finance models discounts as flat SKUs.

Goal: Reduce enterprise procurement lead time by 30% for high-risk customers and standardize commercial levers by building: 1) an automated contract clause generator (templated redlines based on risk tier and region), and 2) an insurance-crediting experiment that offers optional insurance-backed credits in exchange for streamlined SOC2 evidence submission and standardized indemnity limits.

Scope: This PM ticket owns the cross-functional plan to prototype the contract-template generator, define pricing experiments that incorporate insurance credits, and integrate the flow into the vendor procurement portal used by strategic customers. Implementation will touch Legal (clauses), Finance (pricing models), Security (SOC2 evidence acceptance rules), Engineering (portal + template engine), and Design (portal UX).

Non-goals: Do not replace Legal review for custom clauses. This project targets the majority of enterprise deals that currently require modest redlines and insurance adjustments; highly bespoke requests remain handled via existing legal channels.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Contract-template generator integrated with procurement portal that produces PDF redline drafts for 3 common clause families (data residency, liability cap, and audit rights) based on chosen risk tier.
2) Insurance-credit option appears in enterprise quote flow with clear financial mechanics and 3 initial pricing treatments (flat credit, tiered credit, and conditional credit tied to evidence submission).
3) Legal signoff on clause templates and standard terms; Security signoff on SOC2 evidence acceptance checklist.
4) Dashboard metrics instrumented: median procurement lead time, pct deals using insurance credit, and number of clause redlines edited by Legal.
5) Pilot with 4 sales accounts in EMEA/NA with measurable reduction in time-to-sign versus baseline.
milestones: 2025-02-20: Draft PRD and initial clause taxonomy (Legal + Security review)
2025-03-05: Engineering acceptance criteria and API contract for template engine
2025-03-20: Prototype portal flow and pricing experiment variants (Finance)
2025-04-10: Pilot enablement for selected sales accounts
notes:
2025-02-14: Kickoff with Legal (Ava Chen) and Security (Liam O'Connor). Agreed to start with three clause families to limit legal review scope.
2025-02-19: Finance proposed three pricing treatments; prioritized tiered credit experiment first for clearer accounting.
2025-02-25: Eng initial review flagged need for canonical clause metadata (id, variables, jurisdiction). Engineering recommends storing templates in markdown with structured front-matter for deterministic rendering.
2025-02-27: Design mockups show a simplified insurance selector with tooltip explaining tradeoffs; PM requested clearer audit trail exported to contract PDF.
Open trade-offs: whether insurance credits should be refundable if customer fails to submit required artifacts within SLA. Legal prefers non-refundable; Sales prefers conditional refunds. Require Exec alignment before pilot.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (pilot): limited to 4 accounts and two regions; human-in-the-loop Legal review remains mandatory but reduced to approving templates. Phase 2 (scale): automate acceptance for low-risk deals and expose templates to self-serve portal once Legal certifies >80% of edits are unnecessary. Fade insurance-credit experiment into SKU if positive ROI.
Fallback: if legal pushback increases review time, revert to manual workflow and iterate clause content.
measurement: Primary metrics: median procurement lead time (days), pct of deals adopting insurance credit, avg legal redline edits per template, revenue delta for pilot accounts. Success threshold: 30% reduction in lead time and >20% adoption of insurance credit in pilot accounts.
open_questions:
1) Accounting treatment for credits across regions (Finance to confirm).
2) Which jurisdictions permit automated clause insertion without manual notarization? (Legal to confirm).
3) Operational SLA for SOC2 evidence verification to qualify for credits.
4) Policy for refunds if evidence not provided.
